ImageDescription.value:
Qin Dynasty military tally in the shape of a tiger, Shaanxi History Museum

Info provided by the museum shown below:

Bronze Tiger-shaped Tally
Qin Dynasty (221-207BC)
Excavated from Shanmenkou, southern suburbs of Xi'an City
Tally was one kind of special token used by emperor to transmit his order and to confer military power upon his ministers. It is comprised of two halves, the left and the right. The right half was kept in the imperial palace, while the left half was held by commander stationed outside. Only when both parts were fitted together, completing the inscription, would an officer accept the written order as valid.

ImageDescription.value:
Sujet : Fa yuan wen 發 願文. Ling hu Xiu bao 令 狐 烋 寶. nie pan fa shi涅 槃 法 師. Xiao Yan, empereur des Liang, 蕭 衍. Da jiao si 大 覺 寺. Zhi yan 智 嚴. Zhong jing 中 京. Dong du fa yuan wen 東 都 發 願 文, cf.Fa yuan wen. Yi zhu jing zhong xing chan hui yuan wen 依 諸 經 中 行懺 悔 願 文. Colophons

Fa yuan wen 發 願文 Dong du fa yuan wen 東 都 發 願 文, cf.Fa yuan wen. Yi zhu jing zhong xing chan hui yuan wen 依 諸 經 中 行懺 悔 願 文 Numérisation effectuée à partir d'un document de substitution : R 3473. Déb. manque. Titre donné dans le colophon :Dong du fa yuan wen 東 都 發 願 文. Probablement leYi zhu jing zhong xing chan hui yuan wen 依 諸 經 中 行懺 悔 願 文 dont le titre seul est conservé dans le Guanghong ming ji 廣 弘 明 集 (cf. T . 2103, vol. 52, p. 324 a). A la fin du rouleau,colophon : « Dong du fa yuan wen, 1 rouleau,présenté comme offrande aux Ming wang 明 王 (Vidhyārāja) par Zhi yan 智 嚴 (?),maître de la loi du Nirvāna (nie pan fa shi 涅 槃 法師) du monastère Da jue 大 覺 à Zhong jing 中 京, le 1er jour du 5e mois de la 3eannée da tong (25 mai 537)... Copié par Ling huXiu bao 令 狐 烋 寶. » Repr. partielle (col. 41 à 51, 164 à 168 du texte etle colophon) in TKRS , vol.2, pl. 571-2. Cf. AEB ,p. 258. Petite écr., assez élégante, traits descendants à droitefortement appuyés. Quelques car. débordent dans la marge inf. Pour les noms desmembres de la famille impériale et certains termes bouddhiques, le textereprend au déb. de la col. suivante. Rares additions. 172 col. en tout. 22 ou23 col. par f., 17 à 20 car. par col. Marges sup. 3 à 3,6 cm, inf. 3,4 à 3,7cm. Réglure. Fa yuan wen 發 願文 Dong du fa yuan wen 東 都 發 願 文, cf.Fa yuan wen. ImageDescription.value:
As indicated by the end title 觀世音經(Guanshiyin jing), this scroll contains part of the Guanyin Sutra that is based on Chapter 25 of the Lotus Sutra 妙法蓮華經觀世音菩薩普門品第二十五 (Miao fa lian hua jing guan shi yin pu sa pu men pin di er shi wu). The manuscript is made of five sheets of fine yellow paper, with the first one missing its lower right corner. Margins and guidelines divide each sheet into 28 vertical lines of text. There are 17 characters in each row on average (up to 20 characters for parts of the text in verse). The content starts from “得解脫。若有持是觀世音菩薩名(de jie tuo. ruo you chi shi guanshiyin pusa ming)” and stops up at the end of the chapter “阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心 (A nou duo luo san miao san pu ti xin)”. Historical conservation patches made to repair the scroll can be seen on the verso as well. There are repeated water damage marks and losses across the scroll. The manuscript number 's.1609' in black and red ink, the Suzhou numeral 1233 in red crayon and the inscription 觀音經 were recorded on the verso.  These are twentieth-century additions, made after the manuscript was taken from Cave 17, near Dunhuang. The manuscript was recently conserved as part of the Lotus Sutra Manuscripts Digitisation Project and presents several small conservation infills.
This scroll was conserved and digitised as part of the Lotus Sutra Manuscripts Digitisation Project, generously sponsored by the Bei Shan Tang Foundation.

ImageDescription.value:
This scroll fragment is made of a sheet of fine yellow paper to which a small blank piece of paper (the only extant portion of what would have been the protective flap) is still attached.

On the verso, text is regularly written in vertical lines of about 17 characters each that are laid within margins and guidelines. On line 1, the title 妙法蓮華經安樂行品第十四 (Miao fa lian hua jing an le xing pin di shi si) indicates that the manuscript contains part of Chapter 14 of the Lotus Sutra's translation in Chinese by Kumarajiva. The text ends at "不獨他家。若【。。。】 (bu du ta jia. Ruo)". This would have been part of the fifth juan卷五 (juan wu)of the scripture. The verso is blank, except for the number 'S.1058' and the incription 妙法蓮華經安樂行品第十四 - 卷五 and the Suzhou numeral 170, both written in red ink. These are 20th-century additions, made after the manuscript was removed from Mogao Cave 17, near Dunhuang, China.

This scroll was conserved and digitised as part of the Lotus Sutra Manuscripts Digitisation Project, generously sponsored by the Bei Shan Tang Foundation.

The Dahuting Tomb (Chinese: 打虎亭汉墓, Pinyin: Dahuting Han mu; Wade-Giles: Tahut'ing Han mu) of the late Eastern Han Dynasty (25-220 AD), located in Zhengzhou, Henan province, China, was excavated in 1960-1961 and contains vault-arched burial chambers decorated with murals showing scenes of daily life.
For further information, see the Baidu article (in Chinese): 打虎亭汉墓.
Click here for more pictures and a step-by-step walkthrough of the tomb, from the outside, down a stairwell, and through the vaulted burial chambers.

ImageDescription.value:
Millstone and Roller
  • Peiligang Culture
  • Neolithic Period (ca. 5500–5000 B.C.)
  • Excavated at Xinzheng, Henan Province, 1979
A simple block of stone with a flattened surface was used as a millstone, on which the bar was rolled to grind millet and grain into flour. Grains could also be threshed through this process, as it separated husks and chaff from edible parts of the grain.
